title: Customer Comms Templates (Escalation Playbook v2)
author: Dev Patel
content:
## Purpose
These templates are designed to be copy/paste-ready for Support, CSM/TAM, and Engineering to keep customer communication consistent during escalations and incidents.

Use them for:
- Hosted API issues (timeouts, 5xx, streaming disconnects, 429/rate limiting)
- Dedicated capacity shortfalls / latency spikes
- Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) issues (SSO/SAML, networking, audit logs)

## Tone + content guidance (read before sending)
### Do
- Be clear, concise, and specific about what we know *now*.
- Use UTC timestamps or include timezone explicitly.
- Set expectations for the next update time.
- Ask for only the minimum info needed to proceed (request IDs, time range, region, model, correlation IDs).
- Use neutral, customer-centric language (“We’re investigating,” “We’ll update by …”).
- If you don’t know the root cause, say so.

### Don’t
- Don’t promise an RCA unless you are sure the customer is entitled to one and an incident has been declared (see SLA/tier page).
- Don’t promise specific mitigation timelines you can’t control (e.g., “resolved in 15 minutes”). Use “next update by …” instead.
- Don’t speculate about causes (e.g., “GPU failure,” “cloud provider issue”) unless confirmed.
- Don’t provide internal-only details: other customer impact, internal hostnames, shard identifiers, employee names in oncall rotation, internal ticket links, or dashboard screenshots containing other customer names.
- Don’t discuss credits/refunds in the moment. Route to CS leadership per commercial policy.

### What to include in every update (minimum viable update)
- Current status (investigating / identified / mitigating / monitoring / resolved)
- Customer impact (what’s affected + scope)
- Time window (start time, ongoing vs ended)
- What we’re doing now (1–2 bullets)
- What we need from customer (optional)
- Next update time (explicit)

### Status page alignment
If an incident is declared and posted publicly, keep your wording aligned with the status page update.
- Do not contradict the status page.
- If the customer asks for more detail than the status page provides, respond with: “We’re sharing all confirmed details via the status page; we’ll share additional specifics in the post-incident write-up if applicable.”

---

## Standard placeholders (use consistently)
Replace bracketed placeholders before sending.
- [CustomerName]
- [CaseNumber] or [TicketNumber]
- [IncidentID] (if applicable)
- [StartTime] / [EndTime] (include timezone)
- [Region] (e.g., us-east, eu-west)
- [DeploymentMode] (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- [Model] (if relevant)
- [Symptom] (timeouts / 5xx / streaming disconnect / 429 / latency)
- [NextUpdateTime]
- [Workaround] (only if validated + safe-to-share)
- [RequestIDs] or [TimeRange] requested

---

## Template 1 — Investigation started (ack + initial triage)
**When to use:** Immediately after escalation is accepted, or when customer impact is suspected but not confirmed.

**Subject (email):** Update: Investigating [Symptom] on Redwood Inference ([CaseNumber])

**Message:**
Hello [CustomerName],

We’re actively investigating your report of **[Symptom]** affecting **[DeploymentMode]** in **[Region]** (starting around **[StartTime]**).

**Current status:** Investigating

**What we’re doing now:**
- Reviewing service metrics and recent changes related to [component/model/region].
- Correlating your report with request traces using the timestamps you provided.

**To help us isolate the issue**, could you share one of the following (whichever is easiest)?
- 2–3 representative **request IDs** from failed or slow requests, or
- The **time range** (start/end) and the **model** + **region** used, or
- For streaming issues: client library + version and whether you see disconnects during token streaming or before the first token.

We’ll send our next update by **[NextUpdateTime]** (or sooner if we identify a mitigation).

Thank you,
[AgentName]
Redwood Inference Support

---

## Template 2 — Identified (we know what’s wrong, mitigation in progress)
**When to use:** Root cause is narrowed to a component or confirmed failure mode; mitigation is underway.

**Message:**
Hello [CustomerName],

We’ve **identified the cause** of the **[Symptom]** you’re seeing in **[Region]** for **[DeploymentMode]**.

**Current status:** Identified (mitigation in progress)

**What we know so far (confirmed):**
- Impact: [Describe impact succinctly: elevated errors / increased latency / streaming disconnect rate]
- Scope: [e.g., specific region, specific model version, specific Dedicated pool]
- Start time: [StartTime]

**What we’re doing now:**
- [Mitigation step 1 — e.g., routing traffic, rolling back a change, increasing capacity]
- [Mitigation step 2 — e.g., applying config fix, restarting impacted workers]

**Customer action (optional / only if applicable):**
- [Validated workaround]

Next update by **[NextUpdateTime]**.

Thank you,
[AgentName]

---

## Template 3 — Mitigation applied (impact reduced; monitoring)
**When to use:** A mitigation has been deployed and metrics are trending back, but not fully stable or not yet confirmed by the customer.

**Message:**
Hello [CustomerName],

We’ve applied a mitigation to address **[Symptom]** in **[Region]**.

**Current status:** Mitigation applied (monitoring)

**What changed:**
- [One sentence describing the mitigation at a safe-to-share level, e.g., “We adjusted routing/capacity to reduce overload and restore streaming stability.”]

**What we’re seeing now:**
- [Metric trend summary: e.g., error rate returning to baseline / latency improving]

**What we need from you (optional):**
- If you’re able, please confirm whether you’re still seeing issues after **[MitigationTime]**.
- If you still see failures, send 1–2 request IDs from after **[MitigationTime]**.

We will continue monitoring closely and will update you by **[NextUpdateTime]**.

Thank you,
[AgentName]

---

## Template 4 — Monitoring extended (mitigated but not ready to declare resolved)
**When to use:** Things look better but we want a longer observation window (common for latency spikes, intermittent disconnects).

**Message:**
Hello [CustomerName],

We’re continuing to monitor following the mitigation for **[Symptom]** in **[Region]**.

**Current status:** Monitoring

**What we’re observing:**
- [e.g., “Metrics are stable over the last 30 minutes; we’re watching for recurrence during peak load.”]

We’ll provide the next update by **[NextUpdateTime]**, or immediately if the issue recurs.

Thank you,
[AgentName]

---

## Template 5 — Resolved (customer-facing closure)
**When to use:** Incident/escalation is resolved and we have high confidence it won’t recur immediately.

**Message:**
Hello [CustomerName],

This issue is now **resolved**.

**Summary:**
- Symptom: [Symptom]
- Region / deployment: [Region] / [DeploymentMode]
- Impact window: **[StartTime]** to **[EndTime]**

**What we did:**
- [Safe-to-share summary of remediation]

If you notice any recurrence, please reply with a request ID and timestamp and we’ll re-engage immediately.

[Optional RCA language — choose one]
- (RCA provided) We will share a post-incident write-up by **[RCA_DueDate]**.
- (RCA not committed) If you’d like a deeper technical summary, tell us what details would be most helpful and we’ll share what we can.

Thank you for your partnership,
[AgentName]

---

## Template 6 — RCA commitment (only when applicable)
**When to use:** Customer tier/contract requires RCA, or leadership has explicitly committed. Use only after incident is declared or a formal escalation review is opened.

**Message:**
Hello [CustomerName],

We will provide a **post-incident write-up (RCA)** for this event.

**What it will include:**
- Timeline of key events and mitigations
- Confirmed root cause
- Corrective actions (what we’re changing to prevent recurrence)
- Any relevant customer guidance (configuration / retry / fallback recommendations)

**Delivery target:** By **[RCA_DueDate]**.

Note: We’ll share confirmed details only; if any items require additional verification, we’ll call that out explicitly.

Thank you,
[AgentName]

---

## Template 7 — Workaround guidance (validated + safe-to-share)
**When to use:** We have a validated workaround that reduces impact while we fix root cause.

**Message:**
Hello [CustomerName],

While we work on a permanent fix for **[Symptom]**, the following workaround has been validated and should reduce impact:

**Recommended workaround:**
- [Workaround step 1]
- [Workaround step 2]

**Notes / limits:**
- Applies to: [Hosted/Dedicated/Private], [Region], [Model/version]
- Expected effect: [e.g., “reduces disconnect frequency,” “avoids throttling spikes”]
- If you cannot apply this workaround due to constraints, tell us and we’ll propose alternatives.

We will update you by **[NextUpdateTime]** on progress toward a permanent fix.

Thank you,
[AgentName]

---

## Template 8 — Customer update cadence (set expectations)
**When to use:** P0/P1 escalations or high-stakes enterprise conversations where cadence must be explicit.

**Message:**
Hello [CustomerName],

To keep you updated, we will provide investigation updates **every [X] minutes** until we have a mitigation in place, and then **every [Y] hours** while we monitor.

If anything changes materially (mitigation applied, impact worsens, resolution), we will update you immediately rather than waiting for the scheduled time.

Next update by **[NextUpdateTime]**.

Thank you,
[AgentName]

---

## Template 9 — Private deployment / security-sensitive phrasing (SSO, audit logs, networking)
**When to use:** Private/VPC/on-prem issues where details may be restricted or customer environment-specific.

**Message:**
Hello [CustomerName],

We’re investigating the issue affecting your **Private deployment** related to **[SSO/SAML | audit logs | networking | installer/upgrade]**.

**Current status:** Investigating

**What we’re doing now:**
- Reviewing Redwood-side logs and configuration relevant to your tenant/deployment.
- Coordinating with our Security and Private Deployments teams as needed.

**To proceed**, please provide:
- The timestamp of the last known good login/event and the first failure
- Any IdP change window (if applicable) and the IdP error message/correlation ID
- [For networking] NAT/egress IPs, any recent firewall/proxy changes, and the failing endpoint/port

We’ll update you by **[NextUpdateTime]**.

Thank you,
[AgentName]

**Internal note (do not send):** For Private incidents, confirm confidentiality level and avoid sharing any cross-tenant impact. If Security is engaged, route comms through the incident commander or Security incident coordinator.

---

## Template 10 — “We can’t reproduce yet” (request more evidence without sounding blocked)
**When to use:** Customer reports intermittent issues, but our metrics aren’t showing a clear signal.

**Message:**
Hello [CustomerName],

We’re continuing to investigate, but we haven’t yet been able to correlate the issue with our service-side telemetry.

To help us pinpoint it, could you share:
- 2–3 request IDs from impacted calls, and
- The approximate timestamps (including timezone), plus
- Model + region + whether requests were streaming

Once we have that, we can trace the requests end-to-end and determine whether the issue is service-side, network-path related, or client-side.

Next update by **[NextUpdateTime]**.

Thank you,
[AgentName]

---

## Quick “what not to promise” checklist
Before sending, confirm you are NOT implying:
- “RCA guaranteed” (unless explicitly committed)
- “No data loss” / “no security impact” (unless confirmed by Security)
- “We’ll refund credits” / “free month” (route to CS leadership)
- “It’s a cloud provider outage” (unless confirmed + we’re aligned on messaging)
- “We found the bug” (unless root cause is confirmed)

---

## Suggested subject lines (email)
- Update: Investigating [Symptom] in [Region] ([CaseNumber])
- Update: Mitigation in progress for [Symptom] ([CaseNumber])
- Update: Monitoring after mitigation ([CaseNumber])
- Resolved: [Symptom] in [Region] ([CaseNumber])

---

## Channel notes
- **Ticket replies:** Keep the template short; include “Next update by …” every time.
- **Slack Connect:** Use shorter updates and paste the same canonical text as the ticket/email to avoid divergence.
- **Phone/Zoom:** Summarize verbally; immediately follow with a written update using one of the templates to avoid misalignment.

## Ownership and improvements
Owner: Customer Support (Program lead: Dev Patel). Docs partnership: Elliot Price.

If you need a new template for a recurring scenario, file a request in the Escalation Playbook v2 backlog and include:
- Scenario description
- Customer tier(s)
- Safe-to-share constraints
- Example wording that worked / didn’t work
